Ava (Marketing): Quick ask for runtime: we need a reproducible bench pack + sanity verification for the launch assets. Headline numbers (throughput, p50/p95/p99) plus raw artifacts for audit.
Chris (Runtime Eng): Got it. Which models/variants and traffic shapes do you want?
Ava (Marketing): Two model variants: redwood-14b (fp16) and redwood-14b-int8 (quantized). Also include one open-check model (e.g., vicuna-13b) as a public comparator.
Ava (Marketing): Traffic shapes: tiny chat (<=40 tokens), standard reply (<=256 tokens), long doc-summary (<=2048 tokens).
Diego (Runtime Eng): How many requests per cohort? Any warmup rules?
Ava (Marketing): Aim for 1k requests per cohort, 2 repeats. Warmup: 100 requests per worker, deterministic seed for evals. Include a cold-start measurement (single request to a freshly started worker).
Chris (Runtime Eng): We'll run on staging-dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor effects. We'll produce: (1) aggregated metrics (tps, p50/p95/p99, cold-start), (2) raw per-request logs, (3) startup traces if cold-start > 2x typical p95.
Ava (Marketing): Also need cost numbers: headline $/1k tokens using current pricing snapshot, plus raw GPU-seconds and batch sizes in appendix.
Riya (Data Ops): For the reproducibility bundle I need the prompt file and mapping. Ava, can you drop the prompt set link + short curation note?
Ava (Marketing): Prompt set: https://internal.storage/redwood/launch/prompts-v4.txt — 150 prompts, mix of product docs and customer questions, stratified by length. Curation note: removed prompts with personally identifiable info; balanced for token-length buckets.
Diego (Runtime Eng): Please also confirm sampling settings. Do you want streaming vs non-stream?
Ava (Marketing): Sampling: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, deterministic seed 2026 for non-exploratory runs. We want both streaming (for demo) and batch non-stream (for throughput).
Chris (Runtime Eng): Noted. We'll attach exact CLI commands, docker image tags, and seed values. We'll also provide a tiny notebook that reproduces the final headline $/1k tokens from raw logs.
bench-bot: Job queued: bench-job/1716009991. Pool: staging-dedicated-2. ETA run start ~ 30m. :hourglass: 
Ava (Marketing): Can you call out any quantization warmup delta explicitly in the summary? Marketing will highlight if INT8 needs longer warmup or shows cold-start variance.
Diego (Runtime Eng): We'll capture warmup curves (latency vs request index) for INT8 and fp16. If INT8 shows >15% extra warmup cost we'll annotate in the notes.
Riya (Data Ops): I'll prepare the upload location and checksums. Please name artifacts: runid-model-cohort-repeat.jsonl and a README.txt with commands.
Chris (Runtime Eng): Plan: 3 cohorts x 1k requests x 2 repeats x 3 models ~ 18k requests. Estimating ~2 GPU-hours total on staging pool. We'll post artifacts to: s3://redwood-launch/benchpacks/1716009991/ once finished.
Ava (Marketing): ETA for artifacts? We need to review by Friday EOD to freeze deck copy.
Diego (Runtime Eng): If everything goes smoothly we'll have artifacts and a short summary by Thursday EOD; if we hit flaky runs we'll rerun Friday morning and update.
bench-bot: bench-job/1716009991 started on staging-dedicated-2. Status: running.
Chris (Runtime Eng): One more ask: marketing wants a p95 delta table (fp16 vs INT8) per cohort, plus a short note on any numeric regressions found (we'll include exact eval diffs).
Ava (Marketing): Perfect. Also please include the sample indices we used for the deck examples so we can link outputs to the prompt IDs.
Riya (Data Ops): Roger. I'll add prompt-id -> sample-index CSV to the bundle and run SHA256 checksums.
Ava (Marketing): Thanks team. Ping this thread with the s3 links and a 2-sentence summary we can paste into the launch PR. :sparkles:
Diego (Runtime Eng): Will do.
Chris (Runtime Eng): Copy. We'll update when the first run completes.
bench-bot: bench-job/1716009991 completed. Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-launch/benchpacks/1716009991/ (summary.txt, raw-logs.tar.gz, repro-bundle.zip). Checksum files: checksum.txt.
Ava (Marketing): Amazing — downloading now. We'll review and post any follow-ups here. :rocket:
